data.cultural_impact: The name Shuhaib holds significant cultural importance for Muslims. In Islamic history, Shuhaib ibn Amr Al-Khatmi lived during the time of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and was a significant figure who contributed to the spread of Islam, particularly in the region of Yemen. The name has a rich historical background and is revered within the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shuhaib also has deep spiritual significance for Muslims. Shuhaib ibn Amr was known for his unwavering faith and determination to spread the word of Allah, despite facing numerous challenges and adversities in his life. The name, therefore, reminds us of the importance of remaining steadfast in our faith and striving towards our spiritual goals, no matter what obstacles we may face in our personal journeys. Additionally, the name signifies the notion of returning to Allah and seeking His mercy and forgiveness, thus emphasizing the importance of repentance and seeking a closer relationship with Allah.

historical_references.reference: Shuhaib ibn Al-Hanafiyya was a grandson of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the founder of a major Shia Islamic sect known as the Shu'ah or the Shia of Shuhaib. He is considered a leading figure in the early history of Shia Islam.
historical_references.context: Shuhaib was born in Mecca around 610 AD and was a cousin and companion of Imam Husayn. He played a significant role in the establishment of the Zaidi Shia state in Yemen during the late 7th and early 8th centuries.

historical_references.reference: Shuhaib al-Khuzai was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and a prominent figure in early Islam. He is known for his strong faith and his role as a military commander during the early Islamic conquests.
historical_references.context: Shuhaib al-Khuzai was born in Khuzistan, in the Persian Gulf region, and embraced Islam early in the Prophet's mission. He participated in several military campaigns and was appointed as the commander of the army of Kufa during the siege of Hira.
